title: Type Inference, Narrowing & Discriminated Unions
summary: Master type inference, control-flow analysis, type guards (typeof, instanceof, in), custom type predicates, and discriminated unions.
learningObjectives: Perform safe type narrowing using built-in guards and user-defined type predicates (param is Type)
Model complex domain state machines using discriminated unions with exhaustive compile-time checking using never

sections.heading: 1. Control Flow Analysis & Discriminated Union Architecture
sections.content:
TypeScript features a sophisticated Control Flow Analysis engine that tracks types dynamically as execution progresses through conditional branches.

Type Narrowing Mechanisms:
1. `typeof` guards: Narrows primitives (`typeof x === 'string'`).
2. `instanceof` guards: Narrows class instances (`err instanceof DatabaseError`).
3. `in` operator: Narrows objects by property existence (`'token' in payload`).
4. User-Defined Type Predicates: Functions returning `value is SpecificType` to perform custom validation.

Discriminated Unions (Tagged Unions):
The cornerstone of robust domain modeling. A discriminated union consists of multiple interface types that share a single common literal property (the 'discriminant' tag, such as `status` or `kind`).

```typescript
type AsyncState<T> =
  | { status: 'idle' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'success'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: Error };
```

When checking `if (state.status === 'success')`, TypeScript automatically narrows `state` to the exact variant containing `.data`. If you test every case in a switch statement, the default branch can assign the remaining state to `never`:
`const _exhaustiveCheck: never = state;`
If you ever add a new variant (e.g. `{ status: 'cancelled' }`) to the union in the future, the compiler will refuse to build until you handle it in the switch statement!

codeExamples.code:
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| DISCRIMINATED UNION EXHAUSTIVE CONTROL FLOW                       |
|                                                                   |
|  type ApiResponse =                                               |
|    | { status: "success"; data: User }   (Tag: "success")         |
|    | { status: "error"; message: string } (Tag: "error")          |
|                                                                   |
|  switch (response.status) {                                       |
|    case "success":                                                |
|      // TypeScript knows response has .data (Safe!)               |
|      return response.data;                                        |
|    case "error":                                                  |
|      // TypeScript knows response has .message (Safe!)            |
|      return response.message;                                     |
|    default:                                                       |
|      // Compile-time assertion: catches unhandled union cases!     |
|      const _exhaustive: never = response;                         |
|  }                                                                |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
codeExamples.explanation: Checking the shared tag narrows the type. The 'never' check guarantees 100% exhaustive case handling.

keyPoints: Control flow analysis narrows union types automatically within if/switch branches.
Discriminated unions use a common literal tag to distinguish between variants safely.
Assigning unhandled cases to 'never' in default branches creates a compile-time exhaustiveness check.
commonMistakes: Using optional properties on a single bloated object ({ data?, error? }) instead of clean discriminated unions.
Using 'as' type assertions to silence the compiler instead of allowing proper type narrowing to prove safety.

sections.heading: 2. Production Payment State Machine with Exhaustive Check
sections.content: Payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) send polymorphic webhook states. Modeling webhooks as a discriminated union guarantees that developers never read missing transaction IDs on failed charges.

codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates complete type narrowing by tag, accessing variant-specific properties safely with an exhaustive never check.

keyPoints: Discriminated unions make illegal states unrepresentable (e.g. success cannot exist without receiptUrl).
The exhaustive 'never' check provides instant notification during refactoring when a new variant is introduced.
commonMistakes: Omitting the default never check, allowing unhandled union cases to pass silently until runtime crashes.

exercises.title: Build an Exhaustive Order Workflow Engine
exercises.objective: Model order states using a discriminated union and implement an exhaustive transition handler.
exercises.description: Define an OrderStatus discriminated union: PENDING (orderId), SHIPPED (orderId, trackingNumber), DELIVERED (orderId, deliveredAt), and CANCELLED (orderId, reason). Implement formatOrderStatus(status: OrderStatus): string with an exhaustive never check.
instructions: Define OrderStatus union with literal 'status' discriminator.
Write formatOrderStatus using a switch statement.
Implement exhaustive default check assigning to never.
hints: In default case: `const _check: never = order; return _check;`.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Discriminated unions ensure that each order phase only exposes fields valid for that exact status.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the purpose of assigning an unhandled branch to a variable of type 'never' in a switch statement?

options.text: It pauses execution until an asynchronous Promise resolves.
It provides a compile-time check ensuring that all possible variants of a union type have been handled exhaustively.
It instructs the V8 garbage collector to free the variable immediately.
It allows TypeScript to compile to WebAssembly.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: If any union variant is omitted from the switch statement, it falls through to the default branch where assigning it to 'never' causes a compiler error.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is a User-Defined Type Predicate in TypeScript?

options.text: A function that returns a boolean and has a return type signature in the form 'param is Type'.
A regex pattern that validates email strings.
A decorator that checks database permissions.
A tsconfig setting that enables strict null checks.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Type predicates (e.g., 'pet is Dog') inform the compiler's control flow analysis that if the function returns true, the parameter can be safely narrowed to the specified type.

recap: Type narrowing evaluates conditional branches. Discriminated unions with shared literal tags make invalid states impossible and guarantee exhaustive case handling via 'never'.
